Jonas / team,

Bulleted technical response ready — keeping it concise for the customer. High level first, then quick appendix we can attach.

1) Residency guarantees
- For Private/VPC deployments we run the control plane in Redwood's control plane but the inference nodes and object storage (S3-compatible) are provisioned into the customer VPC or their cloud account per contract. Data remains in the provisioned region(s) unless explicit cross-region replication is configured by the customer.
- Backups/snapshots: automated snapshots are retained in the same region by default; we do not enable cross-region replication without customer opt-in.

2) Retention categories
- Transient artifacts: KV cache, inference buffers, and ephemeral logs — default TTL: 72 hours (configurable). These live on encrypted instance-local storage and are purged by the runtime when TTL expires or on pod termination.
- Persisted objects: uploads and user-managed artifacts — retained per customer policy; default lifecycle rules: 365 days unless changed.
- Audit logs/metrics: retention configurable by tenant; default retention in hosted control plane is 90 days for metrics and 1 year for audit logs unless enterprise contract specifies otherwise. For Private deployments, logs can be shipped to customer-managed S3/Cloud Logging and governed by the customer's retention rules.

3) Deletion workflow (customer-initiated) — short form
A) Customer requests deletion via Console API or signed DocuSign request. Request includes account context and resource scoping (all artifacts, or scoped by bucket/prefix).
B) Control plane sends synchronous delete commands to in-VPC object store and inference nodes; we run cross-checks to ensure no in-memory KV cache remains for that tenant.
C) Snapshot lifecycle: delete includes snapshot tombstone + schedule to purge snapshots from object storage; snapshot deletion jobs run asynchronously (within SLA below).
D) Backup retention: if backups are immutable due to legal hold, we mark records and require customer revocation. Otherwise, backups are deleted per the requested scope.
E) Cryptographic keys: if customer uses customer-managed KMS keys, we do not have the ability to decrypt after key destruction; we surface key rotation and destruction timelines as part of the evidence package.

SLA / timelines (proposed)
- Primary object deletion: within 24 hours of verified request.
- Snapshot purge: within 30 days (snapshot GC window to prevent accidental data loss), but can be accelerated with enterprise escalation.
- Audit evidence generation (deletion report and log extracts): within 72 hours.

Attachments: I prepared a short deletion playbook draft (attached) that maps exact commands, playbook steps, and log fields to be exported as proof. I'll share a Drive link for the live doc.

Marissa Cole
Principal Cloud Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Hi Kara —

Thanks for the clear list of questions. Please find our short answers below and an attached draft playbook for your review. If you can confirm the Cerulean account ID and the target environment name (staging vs prod), we will scope the sample artifacts to your environment for proof-of-deletion.

Summary answers (short):
- Residency: Yes — data remains in the customer-specified region(s). We do not enable cross-region replication by default in Private/VPC mode.
- Retention: Transient artifacts default TTL = 72 hours; persisted objects default lifecycle = 365 days (customer-configurable). Audit logs can be delivered to customer-managed storage and retained per customer policy.
- Deletion workflow: Customer request → synchronous delete of active objects → async snapshot GC (default 30-day GC window) → evidence package (audit log slices + deletion manifest) delivered within 72 hours.
- Certificate of deletion: We can provide a signed deletion statement for enterprise customers. See attached "deletion_playbook_draft_v1.pdf" for the certificate template and sample audit log fields.

Action items for Cerulean (what we need from you):
1) Account ID and environment name.
2) Any legal hold exceptions or compliance constraints (e.g., export holds).
3) Preferred evidence delivery channel (Secure Drive link vs SFTP vs KMS-wrapped zipped manifest).

Attached: deletion_playbook_draft_v1.pdf (playbook + sample certificate). Live doc: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/Residency-Deletion-Playbook-v1

If that looks good, we'll generate a scoped sample with your IDs and include a brief runbook of the exact API calls and log extracts.
